SMM-based integrity checking mechanisms are vulnerable to a class of evasion attacks, which we call “evasion attacks” that can defeat the integrity checking mechanisms by removing attack traces before integrity checks and continuing the execution of the attack code after the integrity check is completed.

(1) SMM-based integrity checking mechanisms can be defeated with new evasion attacks that use a compromised software system to remove attack traces before integrity checks are performed; (2) the evasion attacks can be implemented in a few lines of code; and (3) the evasion attacks do not require any hardware modification or special hardware capabilities.

(i) all hardware-based, integrity checking mechanisms that use periodic SMM checks can be defeated by evasion attacks, (ii) SMM-based integrity checking is not an effective defense for malware that is able to compromise a software stack, and (iii) a software-based, integrity checking mechanism is required to provide a complete protection against software-based malware.
